# Supersession: unchanged C# wire checkpoint

`requests-and-synthetic-generation-evidence.zip` contains four independent
1001-row scenarios generated by the official Core test runner. Four tests
passed; its TRX, source observations, scenario timestamps, raw SQLite original,
journal snapshots, request/response hashes and ordered exchanges are inside.
The adjacent manifest pins the ZIP and each scenario manifest.

| Scenario | HTTP requests | Remote work represented during generation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| successor | 27 | Predecessor part 0 accepted; part 1 retired; successor sends only row 1000 |
| retirement_reply_lost | 28 | Same, with part 1 retirement reply dropped and identical retry after restart |
| zerochild | 27 | Both predecessor parts accepted; successor has coverage and no children |
| zerochild_reply_lost | 33 | Same, with empty-plan registration reply dropped, another draft edit, restart and unchanged registration retry |

All 115 request bodies came from production C# DTOs, authentication projection,
HTTP serialization, builder, SQLite and recovery/journal services. Accepted
predecessor events use actual `PosAdminWebClient` apply requests; no ACK is
inserted into the local database to manufacture remote acceptance. The initial
uncertain legacy state is explicitly seeded after the real local import; the
current sender never sends that oversized original to the ordinary endpoint.

**Generation scope:** the response peer remains synthetic. These files do not
prove acceptance by an Admin handler, SQL, live authentication or staging.
Each `*.synthetic-response.json` is labeled accordingly and must not be used as
an expected database response.

The only response-derived canonical hash incorporated in subsequent outgoing
documents is `supersedes.retiredChildren[].canonicalPayloadHash`. During
generation this value is calculated by the actual Admin forensic parser through
its official foundation loader. Every `canonical-child-*.json` pins child JSON,
parser and loader hashes and observed Admin commit
`bee0670a6b9b9fd56d2abb9f29e22ccc45293888`. Parser SHA256:
`f6b22448c3b003685a3791642ec4ef6cc00cdc9175a673eb45d24c8f821f5db4`.
The separate parser projection receives synthetic current credentials; captured
child documents and HTTP bodies are never rewritten. Synthetic root/plan
canonical hashes and ACK UUIDs remain local generation evidence. The outgoing
`supersedes` object contains only `planId` and `retiredChildren`.

For an actual Admin/database replay:

1. Verify the ZIP, scenario manifests and all file hashes before parsing.
2. Use a separate owned isolated database scope for each scenario. All four
   reuse barcodes and synthetic trust IDs; one scenario is not another's seed.
   Shop `10000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000094`, device
   `30000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000094`, session
   `40000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000094`, shop code `FIXTURE`.
3. Execute `exchanges.json` in index order through the real route/handler and
   database. Send each request file unchanged. Requests whose replies were
   dropped still execute remotely; the later retry must reuse its durable result.
4. Capture actual response bytes keyed by scenario, exchange index, route and
   request SHA256. Receipt and retirement may have identical bodies but different
   routes. Report any rejection without repairing the request JSON.
5. Check 1001 distinct products, 2002 distinct price identities and stock 1.25
   per product. Retail for `INTEROP-0` is 1300; `INTEROP-1000` is 1500 in the first
   two scenarios and 1200 in the last two. Other retail values are 1200 and all
   purchase values are 900. Accepted carry must not repeat economic effects;
   zero-child convergence must execute no successor apply. Verify stored plan
   coverage, predecessor retirement fences, receipts and retry equality.

Local checks already passed: original/hash immutable; no new economics before
local commit; first-part operator edit remains a recoverable child draft
(1400, or 1450 after the second lost-reply edit); root closes only after all
needed local ACKs or authoritative empty-plan confirmation. Final local history
counts are 2004 for successor cases and 2003 for zero-child cases. These are
SQLite history counts, not assumed PostgreSQL history row counts.

The source observations in `provenance.json` describe an uncommitted candidate;
the recorded parent commit is not a claim that this product snapshot was
integrated. Future replay receipts must name their own exact Admin source and
SQL state. No shared TEST, deployment or production operation is authorized by
this fixture.
